design_detail: Pooled analysis of eight double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover laboratory studies of MDMA in 139 healthy volunteers (70 men, 69 women), in which people were grouped afterwards by CYP2D6 genotype (activity score; poor, intermediate or extensive metabolizers) and, as a check, by phenotype (dextromethorphan metabolic ratio). The comparison between genotype groups is between persons and the exposure (genotype) is not randomized, although the MDMA sessions were randomized crossovers; the authors call the pooled analysis prospectively designed. Plasma MDMA, MDA and HMMA over time, systolic blood pressure, heart rate, temperature and subjective ratings were compared across groups. The methods, doses, tables and most figures are in a supplement (a PDF file) that was not read.
can_establish: Whether, within healthy adults given MDMA in a laboratory, people with little or no CYP2D6 function differ in blood levels of MDMA and its metabolites and in the timing of blood-pressure and subjective effects from people with normal function, with the size of the difference in the first hours.
cannot_establish: The effect of CYP2D6 genotype at any particular dose (the seven poor metabolizers all took the highest dose and the groups were unevenly spread across studies and doses); effects on toxicity, which no study measured; whether the small difference is caused by MDMA blocking CYP2D6 in everyone, which the authors infer from timing and earlier work and did not test here; or anything about repeated doses, other enzymes or medicines that block CYP2D6.

sample.recruitment: Healthy volunteers from eight earlier studies; recruitment, entry criteria and ages are in the supplement, which was not read. The main text gives only the total (70 men, 69 women) and the genotype groups (Abstract; Results, 3rd paragraph; Fig. 1 legend).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Not given in the main text (supplement not read).
sample.demographics: 70 men and 69 women; ages, weights and the sex mix within genotype groups are not given in the main text.
sample.attrition: Not reported in the main text. HMMA was analysed for 76 people (N=76 in the correlation; F with 73 error degrees of freedom) and unconjugated HMMA for about 124 (inferred from the degrees of freedom), against 139 for MDMA and MDA, with no reason stated.
sample.selection_effects: Healthy volunteers in controlled studies with their own entry criteria. The seven poor metabolizers were all in the high-dose group, and the genotype groups were not equally represented across studies and doses (Discussion, limitations paragraph), so a genotype difference is mixed with dose and study unless the unreported high-dose-only analysis is used.

exposure.measurement: CYP2D6 genotype converted to an activity score (0, 0.5, 1, 2) and to poor, intermediate and extensive groups; phenotype by the urinary ratio of dextromethorphan to its metabolite (DM/DX). Genotype and phenotype were mostly concordant, with some individual discordance (Results, 5th paragraph). Which alleles were scored is in the supplement.
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only: MDMA given once in each study; the doses differ between the eight studies and are not listed in the main text (supplement); all poor metabolizers took the high dose.
exposure.polysubstance: Not described in the main text; the volunteers were healthy and studied in controlled sessions.
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Not described in the main text.

comparison.controls: People with normal CYP2D6 function (extensive metabolizers, activity score 2 in the finer analysis) as the reference group; intermediate metabolizers as a middle group.
comparison.matching: None described. The authors say the groups were unevenly spread across studies and doses and that a high-dose-only analysis gave similar results (not shown in the main text).
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Body weight, sex mix and age per group are not given in the main text. Polymorphisms of CYP1A2, CYP2C19 and CYP2B6 were assessed and the authors say they did not moderate the CYP2D6 effects; those results are to be published separately.

outcomes.instruments: Plasma concentrations of MDMA, its active metabolite MDA and its inactive metabolite HMMA (peak, area under the curve to 6 hours, and the MDMA to HMMA ratio as a marker of CYP2D6 activity); systolic blood pressure, heart rate and body temperature; visual analogue ratings of 'any drug effect' and 'drug liking'.
outcomes.validity_norms: Not discussed in the main text.
outcomes.operationalization: Effects of genotype group at each time point by analysis of variance with post hoc comparisons; early against late differences (before and after 3 hours); correlations between the MDMA to HMMA ratio at 0.6 hours and effects.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None described; the key contrast of peak MDMA between poor and extensive metabolizers has P=0.049 within a main effect of P=0.02.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: The studies were double-blind and placebo-controlled; whether genotype was concealed from those rating effects is not stated in the main text.

analysis.effect_sizes: Peak MDMA in poor metabolizers +15% (mean ratio 1.15, 7 poor against 111 extensive) and peak MDA +50% against extensive metabolizers; peak HMMA 50 to 70% lower, and HMMA exposure to 6 hours about a quarter (24%) of extensive metabolizers' (Abstract; Discussion). Tests: genotype and peak MDMA F(2,136)=4.19, P=0.02, poor against extensive P=0.049; MDMA area under the curve to 6 hours F(2,136)=5.25, P<0.01; MDA peak F(2,136)=8.82, P<0.01 and area F(2,136)=9.09, P<0.001; HMMA peak F(2,73)=3.50, P=0.03 and area F(2,73)=5.22, P<0.01; MDMA to HMMA ratios F(2,73)=10.98 and 10.08, both P<0.001. Systolic pressure rise at 0.6 h greater in poor than in intermediate (P=0.02) and extensive (P=0.01) metabolizers, F(2,135)=3.50, P=0.03; 'any drug effect' higher at 0.6 h (P<0.05); 'drug liking' higher at 0.6 h (P<0.001) and 1 h (P<0.01); no genotype effect on heart rate or temperature; peak effects did not differ. No absolute concentrations are in the main text.
analysis.covariates: None described in the main text; the supplement may contain them.
analysis.preregistration_detail: No registration is mentioned; the authors call the pooled analysis prospectively designed (Introduction, 2nd paragraph) and put the methods in the supplement.
analysis.selective_reporting: The abstract's percentages are not tabulated in the main text, and the tables and most figures are in the supplement. The high-dose-only analysis is described as giving similar results without numbers, and the effects of other CYP polymorphisms are deferred to another paper.
analysis.power: Seven poor metabolizers, all in one dose group; no power calculation. The authors call it the first study with a meaningful sample size and several people with relevantly impaired function.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Compared with extensive metabolizers, the seven poor metabolizers had a peak MDMA level 15% higher and a peak MDA level 50% higher, with much less of the inactive metabolite HMMA; the difference in MDMA was present only up to 3 hours after the dose. Blood pressure and the ratings of drug effect and liking rose faster in poor metabolizers during the first 0.6 to 1 hour, but peak effects, heart rate and temperature did not differ. The main contrast for peak MDMA is borderline (P=0.049).
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract says the effects of CYP2D6 variation are small because MDMA inhibits CYP2D6 itself; the discussion adds that poor metabolizers may be at increased risk of toxicity, that HMMA differences could be clinically relevant, and that other enzymes (CYP2B6, CYP3A4, CYP1A2) may matter more. The self-inhibition explanation is an inference from timing and earlier work, not tested in this analysis; no toxicity outcome was measured; the HMMA and other-enzyme points are speculation. The authors' statement that the differences are small and transient is, however, what the numbers show.

timeline.event: De la Torre et al. reported MDMA pharmacokinetics in one CYP2D6 poor metabolizer and nine extensive metabolizers (named in this paper's reference list; not read here)
A physiologically based model (Yang et al.) estimated that having no CYP2D6 function would raise peak MDMA by only 36%, as the authors cite
Review of MDMA and CYP2D6 pharmacogenetics by the group of the 2000 non-linearity paper
A pooled analysis of trials (Studerus et al., as summarized by Sarparast et al.) found that higher CYP2D6 activity scores predicted lower MDMA levels and that effects followed plasma concentration

replication.where_it_stands: The direction (somewhat higher early MDMA exposure with little or no CYP2D6 function) is consistent with the 2005 case comparison, the 2006 model and the later pooled analysis as summarized by the 2022 review, which quotes larger figures than this paper's main text (19% for peak and 25% for early exposure, comparing only poor metabolizers with only functional alleles; possibly from this paper's supplement, not read). The size at any one dose, and whether MDMA's self-inhibition is the reason the difference is small, rest on this paper and the earlier modelling.

funding.affiliations_note: The last author's group ran the eight pooled studies (Hysek, Vizeli and Liechti among the authors); several of the same group's studies appear in the 2022 review as trials of medicines given before MDMA, so the pooled data and those trials are not independent of each other.

what_would_settle_it: A genotype-stratified crossover in which people with no, intermediate and normal CYP2D6 function (genotyped and phenotyped) take the same dose in randomized, blinded order, enough poor metabolizers of each sex to give interval estimates, with CYP2B6, CYP1A2, CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 status and a CYP3A4 or pan-CYP inhibitor arm, and with temperature, sodium and clinical outcomes as well as concentrations.

domains.note: Provisional: dose and study are unevenly spread across genotype groups and all seven poor metabolizers were in the high-dose group; a high-dose-only analysis is said to give similar results but is not shown, and covariate adjustment is not described in the main text. Genotype itself is not open to the usual confounders.

domains.domain: Bias in measurement of the exposure
domains.note: Genotype and phenotype were both measured, with some discordance in individuals; the main results use genotype groups and phenotype was used as a check.

domains.domain: Bias in selection of participants into the study
domains.note: Volunteers from eight studies with their own entry criteria, not described in the main text; healthy adults only; no sign that selection depended on genotype.
The exposure is genotype, which cannot be changed by later events; the MDMA conditions analysed are described as placebo-controlled sessions.

HMMA statistics rest on about 76 and unconjugated HMMA on about 124 of 139 people (counts inferred from the degrees of freedom and the N=76 of the correlation), with no reason or check for differences between genotype groups.

domains.domain: Bias in measurement of the outcome
domains.note: Plasma concentrations are objective; ratings came from double-blind sessions.

domains.domain: Bias in selection of the reported result
domains.note: Many outcomes and time points without multiplicity control; the key contrast has P=0.049; the abstract's percentages, tables and sensitivity analyses are not in the main text; other CYP results deferred.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: The exposure and outcomes are measured objectively and the finding is modest and in the expected direction, but only seven people have no CYP2D6 function, all took the same high dose, and the covariate handling and sensitivity analysis are in a supplement that was not read, so the overall judgment is provisional. The source can be cited for a small and short-lived rise in peak MDMA (about 15%) and a larger rise in MDA, much less HMMA, and faster early blood-pressure and subjective effects in people with no CYP2D6 function, in healthy adults in the laboratory; it cannot be cited for the effect at a given dose, for intermediate metabolizers as a separate group with precision, for toxicity or for the mechanism.

key_findings.finding: Pooled analysis of eight double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover studies in 139 healthy people (70 men, 69 women): 7 CYP2D6 poor metabolizers, 19 intermediate and 113 extensive metabolizers (111 extensive in one Discussion comparison). Doses and study details are in the supplement (not read); all seven poor metabolizers were in the high-dose group.
key_findings.locator: Abstract; Main text, 2nd paragraph; Fig. 1 legend; Discussion, limitations paragraph

key_findings.finding: Genotype altered MDMA levels only in the first 3 hours (absorption and distribution), not after: genotype main effect on peak MDMA F(2,136)=4.19, P=0.02, with higher peaks in poor than extensive metabolizers (P=0.049); area under the curve to 6 hours F(2,136)=5.25, P<0.01 (poor higher than extensive, P<0.01). Peak MDMA was 15% higher in poor metabolizers (abstract) and the mean ratio was 1.15 (7 poor against 111 extensive).
key_findings.locator: Abstract; Main text, 3rd paragraph; Discussion, 'Taken together' paragraph

key_findings.finding: The active metabolite MDA was higher and the inactive metabolite HMMA lower in poor metabolizers: peak MDA +50% (F(2,136)=8.82, P<0.01; area F=9.09, P<0.001; higher than both intermediate and extensive, P<0.001); peak HMMA 50 to 70% lower (F(2,73)=3.50, P=0.03; area F=5.22, P<0.01), with HMMA exposure to 6 hours about a quarter (24%) of extensive metabolizers'; MDMA to HMMA ratios higher in poor metabolizers (F(2,73)=10.98 and 10.08, P<0.001). The HMMA tests rest on fewer people than the MDMA and MDA tests (N=76 in the HMMA correlation and 73 error degrees of freedom, against 136).
key_findings.locator: Abstract; Main text, 3rd paragraph; Discussion, 'Taken together' paragraph; Fig. 1 legend

key_findings.finding: Poor metabolizers had faster early effects but not larger ones: systolic pressure rise greater than in intermediate (P=0.02) and extensive (P=0.01) metabolizers at 0.6 h (F(2,135)=3.50, P=0.03), 'any drug effect' higher at 0.6 h (P<0.05) and 'drug liking' higher at 0.6 h (P<0.001) and 1 h (P<0.01); maximal effects did not differ and there was no genotype effect on heart rate or temperature. The MDMA to HMMA ratio at 0.6 h correlated with systolic pressure rise (Rs=0.41, N=76), any drug effect (0.42) and drug liking (0.40), all P<0.001.
key_findings.locator: Abstract; Main text, 4th paragraph; Fig. 2 legend

key_findings.finding: The authors read the small and short-lived difference as the result of MDMA inhibiting CYP2D6 itself (turning all people into functional poor metabolizers within about 1 hour); they cite a physiologically based model estimating a rise of only 36% in peak MDMA with no CYP2D6 function, and say medicines that inhibit CYP2D6 raised peak MDMA by 15 to 20% and exposure by 10 to 30% (their references 6 and 7: reboxetine and duloxetine). They note that poor metabolizers were not over-represented in ecstasy deaths (their reference 11), that severe or fatal toxicity with high MDMA exposure occurred with ritonavir (which blocks CYP2D6, CYP2B6 and CYP3A4), and suggest that other enzymes and CYP3A4 inhibition may matter more than CYP2D6 genetics.
key_findings.locator: Discussion, 'Taken together' paragraph (also the following paragraph on limitations)

key_findings.finding: Stated limits: a pooled sample of different studies and doses, unequal representation of activity groups across studies and doses, only seven poor metabolizers and all in the high-dose group; an analysis of the high-dose group alone is said to give similar results (not shown).

reporting_issues.issue: The percentages in the abstract (peak MDMA +15%, peak MDA +50%, peak HMMA 50 to 70% lower) are not given in the main text except as a mean ratio of 1.15 for MDMA and a 24% HMMA exposure; the tables and group means are in the supplement.
reporting_issues.consequence: The sizes cannot be checked against absolute concentrations from the main text; they are quoted as the authors state them.

reporting_issues.issue: The Discussion compares 7 poor metabolizers with 111 extensive metabolizers, but the figure legends and the groups sum to 113 extensive metabolizers (7 + 19 + 113 = 139).
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor: two extensive metabolizers are unaccounted for in one comparison; the reason is not stated.

reporting_issues.issue: The 2022 review of interactions (Sarparast et al.) states that poor metabolizers with only *3, *4 or *5 alleles had a peak 19% and early exposure 25% higher than extensive metabolizers with only *1 and *2 alleles, citing this paper; the main text here gives 15% against all extensive metabolizers and no exposure percentage.
reporting_issues.consequence: The review's figures probably come from the activity-score tables in the supplement; the two sets should not be mixed, and the 15% figure is the one the main text supports.

reporting_issues.issue: A rank correlation of 0.18 between MDMA and MDA exposure is described as showing that higher MDMA levels resulted in higher MDA levels.
reporting_issues.consequence: A weak association (about 3% of rank variance) is given a causal verb; it is a description of co-variation in a pooled sample.

reporting_issues.issue: The main contrast for peak MDMA (poor against extensive) is P=0.049 within a main effect of P=0.02, among many outcomes and time points with no correction for multiplicity; the pooled data come from different studies and doses.
reporting_issues.consequence: The 15% difference in peak MDMA is a borderline finding; the more robust signals are the metabolite differences and the early-time effects.

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC4949007 (main text, figure legends and reference list read as text; Figures 1 and 2 not viewed as images; the supplementary file, a PDF with the methods and tables, was not read, being a download)
